entries.overview: A broad, thin muscle sheet covering the forehead just beneath the skin.
entries.function: Pulls the scalp forward and lifts the eyebrows to wrinkle the forehead in surprise or focus.

details.origin: Tendon sheet over the top of the skull (epicranial aponeurosis)
details.insertion: Skin of the eyebrows and circular eye muscle (orbicularis oculi)
details.innervation: Facial nerve (cranial nerve VII, temporal branch)
details.action: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of Facial Expression
Wikipedia — Frontalis muscle

entries.overview: A ring-shaped sphincter muscle encircling the mouth inside the upper and lower lips.
entries.function: Closes, purses, and protrudes the lips during speaking, whistling, eating, and kissing.

details.origin: Upper jaw (maxilla), lower jaw (mandible), and surrounding facial muscles
details.insertion: Skin and corners around the lips
details.innervation: Facial nerve (cranial nerve VII, buccal branch)
details.action: Closes, compresses, and puckers the lips

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of Facial Expression
Wikipedia — Orbicularis oris muscle

entries.overview: A diagonal strap muscle running from the cheekbone down to the corner of the mouth.
entries.function: Draws the corners of the mouth upward and outward to create a broad smile.

details.origin: Front surface of the cheekbone (zygomatic bone)
details.insertion: Corner of the mouth (modiolus)
details.innervation: Facial nerve (cranial nerve VII, zygomatic and buccal branches)
details.action: Pulls the mouth corners upward and outward

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of Facial Expression
Wikipedia — Zygomaticus major muscle

entries.overview: A large, fan-shaped chewing muscle filling the shallow temple hollow on each side of the skull.
entries.function: Pulls the lower jaw upward and backward to clamp the teeth shut and retract the chin.

details.origin: Temple lines on the side skull bone (parietal bone) and sphenoid bone
details.insertion: Front bony projection (coronoid process) of the lower jawbone (mandible)
details.innervation: Deep temporal branches of the mandibular nerve (cranial nerve V3)
details.action: Elevates and retracts the lower jaw

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Lower Jaw
Wikipedia — Temporalis muscle

entries.overview: The thick, rectangular outer layer of the main jaw-closing muscle over the side of the cheek.
entries.function: Generates strong biting force by lifting and slightly thrusting forward the lower jaw.

details.origin: Cheekbone arch (zygomatic arch) and front cheekbone (zygomatic bone)
details.insertion: Outer angle and rear vertical part (ramus) of the lower jawbone (mandible)
details.action: Elevates and protrudes the lower jaw during chewing

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Lower Jaw
Wikipedia — Masseter muscle

entries.overview: A broad, paper-thin sheet of superficial muscle draped across the front and sides of the neck.
entries.function: Tenses the neck skin and pulls the corners of the mouth and lower lip downward.

details.origin: Connective tissue over the upper chest and front shoulder just below the collarbone (clavicle)
details.insertion: Lower rim of the lower jawbone (mandible), cheek skin, and corners of the mouth
details.innervation: Facial nerve (cranial nerve VII, cervical branch)
details.bloodSupply: Branches of the submental and suprascapular arteries
details.action: Depresses the mouth corners and lower lip while tensing the neck skin

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of Facial Expression
Wikipedia — Platysma muscle

entries.overview: A prominent, two-headed cord running diagonally from the top of the chest to behind each ear.
entries.function: Turns the head toward the opposite shoulder when one side contracts, or nods the head forward together.

details.origin: Top of the breastbone (manubrium of sternum) and inner third of the collarbone (clavicle)
details.insertion: Bony bump behind the ear (mastoid process of temporal bone) and rear skull ridge
details.innervation: Spinal accessory nerve (cranial nerve XI, motor) and C2–C3 cervical nerves
details.action: Turns the head to the opposite side, tilts the neck to the same side, and flexes the neck

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Head
Wikipedia — Sternocleidomastoid muscle

entries.overview: The broad, triangular upper portion of the trapezius spanning from the base of the skull to the shoulder.
entries.function: Shrugs and raises the shoulder blade upward and helps tilt the head backward.

details.origin: Back of the skull (occipital bone), nuchal ligament, and spinous processes of neck vertebrae
details.insertion: Outer third of the collarbone (clavicle), shoulder tip (acromion), and spine of the shoulder blade (scapula)
details.innervation: Accessory nerve (cranial nerve XI) and C3–C4 spinal nerves
details.action: Elevates and rotates the shoulder blade upward and assists neck extension

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Position the Pectoral Girdle
Wikipedia — Trapezius

entries.overview: A wide, fan-shaped muscle covering the middle and lower back and tapering up into the armpit.
entries.function: Pulls the raised arm downward and backward during climbing, swimming, and rowing.

details.origin: Spinous processes of T7–L5 vertebrae, lower 4 ribs, hip crest (iliac crest), and shoulder blade tip
details.insertion: Front groove near the top of the upper arm bone (humerus)
details.bloodSupply: Thoracodorsal branch of the subscapular artery
details.action: Extends, adducts, and internally rotates the arm at the shoulder

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Humerus
Wikipedia — Latissimus dorsi muscle

entries.overview: A flat, diamond-shaped upper-back muscle lying beneath the trapezius between the spine and shoulder blade.
entries.function: Squeezes the shoulder blades together toward the spine and holds them flat against the ribcage.

details.origin: Spinous processes of thoracic vertebrae T2–T5
details.insertion: Inner border of the shoulder blade (scapula)
details.action: Retracts, stabilizes, and rotates the shoulder blade downward

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Position the Pectoral Girdle
Wikipedia — Rhomboid major muscle

entries.overview: The middle, longest column of the deep back extensors running along the thoracic spine and lower ribs.
entries.function: Keeps the spine upright against gravity, extends the back, and bends the trunk sideways.

details.origin: Lumbar vertebrae transverse processes and deep lower back tendon sheet (thoracolumbar fascia)
details.insertion: Transverse processes of all thoracic vertebrae and the lower nine or ten ribs
details.innervation: Posterior branches of thoracic and lumbar spinal nerves
details.bloodSupply: Segmental branches of posterior intercostal, lumbar, and lateral sacral arteries
details.action: Extends the vertebral column and bends the trunk to the same side

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of the Posterior Neck and Back
Wikipedia — Longissimus

entries.overview: The large, fan-shaped chest portion of the pectoralis major running from the breastbone to the upper arm.
entries.function: Brings the arm across the chest, rotates the arm inward, and pulls a raised arm forcefully downward.

details.origin: Front of the breastbone (sternum), upper six rib cartilages, and abdominal tendon sheet
details.insertion: Outer ridge of the upper groove of the upper arm bone (humerus)
details.bloodSupply: Pectoral branch of the thoracoacromial trunk
details.action: Adducts, extends from flexion, and internally rotates the arm

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Humerus
Wikipedia — Pectoralis major

entries.overview: A thin, triangular chest muscle hidden directly behind the larger pectoralis major.
entries.function: Draws the shoulder blade forward and downward around the ribcage and helps lift the ribs when inhaling.

details.origin: Outer front surfaces of ribs 3–5 near their cartilage junctions
details.insertion: Front hook-like projection (coracoid process) of the shoulder blade (scapula)
details.bloodSupply: Pectoral branch of the thoracoacromial trunk
details.action: Protracts and depresses the shoulder blade and assists deep inhalation

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Position the Pectoral Girdle
Wikipedia — Pectoralis minor

entries.overview: A saw-toothed muscle wrapping from the side of the upper ribcage backward beneath the shoulder blade.
entries.function: Pulls the shoulder blade forward during punching or pushing and rotates it upward to raise the arm overhead.

details.origin: Outer surfaces of the upper ribs 1–9 along the side of the chest
details.insertion: Inner front edge of the shoulder blade (scapula)
details.bloodSupply: Lateral thoracic, superior thoracic, and thoracodorsal arteries
details.action: Protracts, stabilizes, and upwardly rotates the shoulder blade

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Position the Pectoral Girdle
Wikipedia — Serratus anterior muscle

entries.overview: A broad, dome-shaped internal sheet of skeletal muscle separating the chest cavity from the abdomen.
entries.function: Serves as the primary muscle of breathing by flattening downward to draw air into the lungs.

details.origin: Lower tip of breastbone (xiphoid process), lower ribs 6–12, and lumbar vertebrae L1–L3
details.insertion: Central dome tendon in the middle of the chest floor (central tendon of diaphragm)
details.innervation: Phrenic nerves (C3–C5) and lower intercostal nerves
details.bloodSupply: Pericardiacophrenic, musculophrenic, and inferior phrenic arteries
details.action: Flattens on contraction to expand chest volume during inhalation

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of the Thorax
Wikipedia — Thoracic diaphragm

entries.overview: Eleven pairs of thin muscular sheets slanting downward and forward between neighboring ribs.
entries.function: Lift the ribcage upward and outward during breathing in, widening the chest cavity.

details.origin: Lower border of each rib above
details.insertion: Upper border of the next rib below
details.action: Elevates the ribs to expand the chest during inhalation

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of the Thorax
Wikipedia — External intercostal muscles

entries.overview: A paired strap muscle running vertically along the front of the belly wall, divided by fibrous bands.
entries.function: Curls the ribcage toward the pelvis during sit-ups and stabilizes the lower spine against arching.

details.origin: Front upper ridge of the pubic bone (hip bone)
details.insertion: Cartilages of ribs 5–7 and lower tip of the breastbone (xiphoid process)
details.action: Flexes the lumbar spine and compresses the abdominal wall

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of the Abdomen
Wikipedia — Rectus abdominis muscle

entries.overview: The largest and most superficial of the three layered flank muscles wrapping the sides of the abdomen.
entries.function: Compresses the abdomen, bends the torso sideways, and twists the chest toward the opposite hip.

details.origin: Outer surfaces of the lower eight ribs (ribs 5–12)
details.insertion: Midline abdominal tendon (linea alba), pubic crest, and outer front hip crest (iliac crest)
details.bloodSupply: Lower intercostal, deep circumflex iliac, and iliolumbar arteries
details.action: Flexes the trunk, twists the torso to the opposite side, and compresses the abdomen

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of the Abdomen
Wikipedia — Abdominal external oblique muscle

entries.overview: The middle sheet of the side abdominal wall, whose fibers fan upward at right angles to the outer oblique.
entries.function: Supports the abdominal organs, bends the waist sideways, and rotates the torso toward the same side.

details.origin: Groin ligament (inguinal ligament), hip crest (iliac crest), and lower back fascia
details.insertion: Lower ribs 10–12, midline abdominal tendon (linea alba), and pubic crest
details.innervation: Thoracoabdominal (T7–T11), subcostal (T12), iliohypogastric, and ilioinguinal nerves
details.action: Compresses abdominal contents and rotates the trunk toward the same side

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of the Abdomen
Wikipedia — Abdominal internal oblique muscle

entries.overview: The deepest layer of the belly wall, running horizontally around the midsection like a built-in corset.
entries.function: Draws the belly inward to increase core stiffness before movement and protect the lower back.

details.origin: Hip crest (iliac crest), groin ligament, lower back fascia, and costal cartilages 7–12
details.insertion: Midline abdominal tendon (linea alba), lower breastbone tip, and pubic crest
details.innervation: Thoracoabdominal (T6–T11), subcostal (T12), iliohypogastric, and ilioinguinal nerves
details.bloodSupply: Subcostal and deep circumflex iliac arteries
details.action: Compresses the abdominal cavity and stabilizes the core

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of the Abdomen
Wikipedia — Transverse abdominal muscle

entries.overview: A thick, four-sided deep lower-back muscle bridging the back of the pelvis to the lowest rib.
entries.function: Hikes one hip upward, bends the lower spine sideways, and anchors the twelfth rib during deep breaths.

details.origin: Back inner border of the hip bone crest (iliac crest)
details.insertion: Lower edge of the twelfth rib and transverse processes of lumbar vertebrae L1–L4
details.innervation: Subcostal nerve (T12) and anterior branches of lumbar nerves L1–L4
details.bloodSupply: Lumbar arteries and lumbar branch of the iliolumbar artery
details.action: Side-bends the lumbar spine and stabilizes the twelfth rib

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of the Abdomen
Wikipedia — Quadratus lumborum muscle

entries.overview: A hammock-like band of the pelvic floor stretching from the front pubic bone back toward the tailbone.
entries.function: Cradles the bladder, uterus, or prostate and tightens around pelvic openings to maintain continence.

details.origin: Inner back surface of the pubic bone (hip bone) inside the pelvis
details.insertion: Tailbone (coccyx) and central pelvic ligament line
details.innervation: Levator ani nerve (S4) and inferior rectal branch of pudendal nerve (S3–S4)
details.bloodSupply: Inferior gluteal and internal pudendal arteries
details.action: Supports pelvic organs and helps control bladder and bowel outlets

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles of the Pelvic Floor
Wikipedia — Levator ani

entries.overview: The thick, rounded middle portion of the shoulder cap muscle spanning directly over the top of the joint.
entries.function: Serves as the main mover that lifts the entire arm straight out to the side after the first few degrees.

details.origin: Outer bony roof of the shoulder tip (acromion of scapula)
details.insertion: Mid-outer bump on the upper arm bone (deltoid tuberosity of humerus)
details.bloodSupply: Thoracoacromial and posterior circumflex humeral arteries
details.action: Abducts the arm outward away from the torso

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Humerus
Wikipedia — Deltoid muscle

entries.overview: A deep rotator-cuff muscle resting in the top trough on the back of the shoulder blade.
entries.function: Starts lifting the arm out to the side and pulls the ball of the arm bone snugly into its socket.

details.origin: Upper hollow above the spine on the back of the shoulder blade (scapula)
details.insertion: Topmost facet on the outer knob of the upper arm bone (greater tubercle of humerus)
details.action: Initiates arm abduction and stabilizes the shoulder joint

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Humerus
Wikipedia — Supraspinatus muscle

entries.overview: A thick, triangular rotator-cuff muscle filling the broad hollow below the ridge of the shoulder blade.
entries.function: Rotates the arm outward and prevents the shoulder head from sliding forward during throwing or reaching.

details.origin: Broad lower hollow on the back of the shoulder blade (scapula)
details.insertion: Middle facet on the outer knob of the upper arm bone (greater tubercle of humerus)
details.action: Externally rotates the arm and stabilizes the shoulder joint

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Humerus
Wikipedia — Infraspinatus muscle

entries.overview: A large, flat rotator-cuff muscle lining the front ribs-facing surface of the shoulder blade.
entries.function: Twists the upper arm inward and acts as a muscular shield stabilizing the front of the shoulder socket.

details.origin: Smooth front hollow facing the ribs on the shoulder blade (scapula)
details.insertion: Front knob on the upper arm bone (lesser tubercle of humerus)
details.action: Internally rotates and adducts the arm while stabilizing the shoulder

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Humerus
Wikipedia — Subscapularis muscle

entries.overview: The outer belly of the prominent two-headed muscle along the front of the upper arm.
entries.function: Bends the elbow, turns the forearm palm-up, and steadies the top of the arm bone inside the shoulder.

details.origin: Small bump just above the shoulder socket on the shoulder blade (scapula)
details.insertion: Upper bump of the forearm radius bone and forearm fascia
details.action: Flexes the elbow, supinates the forearm, and assists shoulder flexion

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Forearm
Wikipedia — Biceps

entries.overview: A powerful muscle lying deep beneath the biceps across the lower half of the front upper arm.
entries.function: Acts as the strongest pure flexor of the elbow regardless of whether the palm faces up or down.

details.origin: Lower half of the front surface of the upper arm bone (humerus)
details.insertion: Front hook and rough bump near the top of the inner forearm bone (ulna)
details.innervation: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C7) and a small branch of the radial nerve
details.action: Flexes the elbow joint

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Forearm
Wikipedia — Brachialis muscle

entries.overview: The inner, longest head of the three-part muscle filling the back of the upper arm.
entries.function: Straightens the bent elbow and pulls the raised upper arm backward toward the ribs.

details.origin: Bony bump just beneath the shoulder socket on the shoulder blade (scapula)
details.insertion: Point of the elbow at the top back of the inner forearm bone (olecranon of ulna)
details.bloodSupply: Deep brachial and posterior circumflex humeral arteries
details.action: Extends the elbow and assists extension and adduction at the shoulder

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Forearm
Wikipedia — Triceps

entries.overview: A long muscle bridging the outer lower upper arm and the thumb side of the forearm.
entries.function: Bends the elbow forcefully when the hand is held in a neutral thumbs-up handshake position.

details.origin: Lower outer ridge of the upper arm bone (humerus)
details.insertion: Thumb-side tip near the wrist end of the outer forearm bone (radius)
details.action: Flexes the elbow and brings a rotated forearm back toward mid-position

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Forearm
Wikipedia — Brachioradialis

entries.overview: A slender superficial muscle running diagonally down the palm side of the forearm toward the thumb side.
entries.function: Bends the wrist forward toward the palm and tilts the hand toward the thumb side.

details.origin: Inner bony bump near the elbow end of the upper arm bone (humerus)
details.insertion: Bases of the second and third hand bones (metacarpals)
details.action: Flexes and abducts the wrist toward the thumb side

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Wrist, Hand, and Fingers
Wikipedia — Flexor carpi radialis muscle

entries.overview: A deep, spindle-shaped muscle running alongside the lower spine across the front of the hip joint.
entries.function: Lifts the thigh forward when walking or climbing stairs and tilts the lower back forward when standing.

details.origin: Sides and discs of thoracic vertebra T12 through lumbar vertebrae L1–L5
details.insertion: Inner upper knob near the top of the thigh bone (lesser trochanter of femur)
details.innervation: Anterior branches of lumbar spinal nerves L1–L3
details.bloodSupply: Lumbar branch of the iliolumbar artery
details.action: Flexes the hip joint and helps stabilize the lumbar spine

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Psoas major muscle

entries.overview: The largest and outermost muscle of the buttock, shaping the rear contour of the hip.
entries.function: Drives the thigh backward when standing up from a chair, climbing stairs, or sprinting.

details.origin: Rear outer blade of the hip bone (ilium), sacrum, tailbone (coccyx), and sacrotuberous ligament
details.insertion: Upper rear ridge of the thigh bone (femur) and outer thigh band (iliotibial tract)
details.action: Extends and externally rotates the thigh at the hip

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Gluteus maximus

entries.overview: A broad, fan-shaped muscle covering the outer side of the pelvis, partly hidden under gluteus maximus.
entries.function: Lifts the leg out to the side and keeps the pelvis level on the standing leg with every step.

details.origin: Outer side surface of the upper hip bone (ilium)
details.insertion: Outer hip knob at the top of the thigh bone (greater trochanter of femur)
details.action: Abducts the thigh and stabilizes the pelvis during walking

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Gluteus medius

entries.overview: A flat, triangular inner-thigh muscle spanning from the front pelvis down to the middle thigh shaft.
entries.function: Squeezes the thighs together and assists bringing the leg forward during kicking or striding.

details.origin: Front body of the pubic bone just below the pubic crest (hip bone)
details.insertion: Middle third of the rear ridge along the thigh bone (linea aspera of femur)
details.innervation: Anterior branch of the obturator nerve (L2–L4)
details.action: Adducts and assists flexion at the hip

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Adductor longus muscle

entries.overview: A massive, fan-shaped muscle forming the deep muscular bulk of the inner thigh.
entries.function: Draws the thigh forcefully inward while its rear portion helps extend the hip during standing and running.

details.origin: Lower pubic rim and sitting bone (ischial tuberosity of hip bone)
details.insertion: Rear ridge and lower inner bump of the thigh bone (femur)
details.innervation: Posterior branch of the obturator nerve and tibial part of the sciatic nerve
details.action: Adducts the thigh and assists both hip flexion and hip extension

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Adductor magnus muscle

entries.overview: The longest muscle in the human body, curving diagonally like a ribbon across the front of the thigh.
entries.function: Flexes, lifts out, and turns out the hip while bending the knee to sit cross-legged.

details.origin: Front upper corner of the hip bone (anterior superior iliac spine)
details.insertion: Upper inner front surface of the shinbone (tibia)
details.action: Flexes, abducts, and externally rotates the hip and flexes the knee

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Sartorius muscle

entries.overview: The central, straight muscle of the quadriceps group running straight down the front of the thigh.
entries.function: Straightens the knee when kicking and helps lift the straight leg forward at the hip.

details.origin: Front hip notch (anterior inferior iliac spine) and upper hip socket rim (hip bone)
details.insertion: Kneecap (patella) and upper shinbone bump (tibial tuberosity) via the quadriceps tendon
details.bloodSupply: Descending branch of the lateral femoral circumflex artery
details.action: Extends the knee and flexes the thigh at the hip

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Rectus femoris muscle

entries.overview: The largest and outermost muscle of the four-part quadriceps along the outer front thigh.
entries.function: Powers knee extension during walking, jumping, squatting, and rising from a seated position.

details.origin: Upper outer hip knob (greater trochanter) and outer rear shaft of the thigh bone (femur)
details.insertion: Kneecap (patella) and upper shinbone (tibia) through the quadriceps tendon
details.action: Extends and stabilizes the knee joint

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Vastus lateralis muscle

entries.overview: A teardrop-shaped quadriceps muscle hugging the inner lower front of the thigh just above the knee.
entries.function: Straightens the knee through the final degrees of locking and keeps the kneecap tracking centrally.

details.origin: Inner line and shaft of the thigh bone (femur)
details.insertion: Inner upper border of the kneecap (patella) and quadriceps tendon
details.action: Extends the knee and stabilizes kneecap tracking

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Vastus medialis

entries.overview: The long outer hamstring muscle stretching down the back of the thigh from the sitting bone to the knee.
entries.function: Drives the thigh backward at the hip and bends and slightly turns outward the bent knee.

details.origin: Lower sitting bone bump of the pelvis (ischial tuberosity of hip bone)
details.insertion: Head of the outer lower leg bone (fibula)
details.innervation: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L5–S2)
details.bloodSupply: Perforating branches of the deep femoral artery
details.action: Extends the hip, flexes the knee, and laterally rotates the flexed knee

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Biceps femoris muscle

entries.overview: A fusiform inner hamstring muscle along the back of the thigh whose lower half tapers into a long cord-like tendon.
entries.function: Extends the hip backward while running and bends and rotates inward the flexed knee.

details.origin: Lower sitting bone bump of the pelvis (ischial tuberosity of hip bone)
details.insertion: Upper inner front surface of the shinbone (tibia)
details.innervation: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L5–S2)
details.action: Flexes the knee, medially rotates the flexed knee, and extends the hip

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Gluteal and Thigh Muscles
Wikipedia — Semitendinosus muscle

entries.overview: The prominent inner belly of the superficial calf muscle forming the upper contour behind the lower leg.
entries.function: Points the toes downward to push off during walking, running, and jumping, and assists knee bending.

details.origin: Back surface above the inner lower knob of the thigh bone (medial condyle of femur)
details.insertion: Heel bone (calcaneus) via the Achilles tendon
details.bloodSupply: Sural branches of the popliteal artery
details.action: Plantar flexes the ankle and assists knee flexion

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Feet and Toes
Wikipedia — Gastrocnemius muscle

entries.overview: A broad, flat calf muscle lying directly beneath the gastrocnemius from just below the knee to the heel.
entries.function: Provides steady downward ankle power for standing upright and pushing off at every walking stride.

details.origin: Back upper shaft of both the shinbone (tibia) and outer lower leg bone (fibula)
details.insertion: Heel bone (calcaneus) via the Achilles tendon
details.bloodSupply: Popliteal, posterior tibial, and fibular arteries
details.action: Plantar flexes the ankle and steadies the leg over the foot

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Feet and Toes
Wikipedia — Soleus muscle

entries.overview: The fleshy muscle running right beside the sharp front crest on the outer side of the shinbone.
entries.function: Pulls the front of the foot upward so the toes clear the ground during each forward step.

details.origin: Upper outer shaft of the shinbone (tibia) and connecting membrane
details.insertion: Inner arch bones of the midfoot (medial cuneiform and first metatarsal)
details.action: Lifts the foot upward (dorsiflexion) and turns the sole inward (inversion)

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Muscles That Move the Feet and Toes
Wikipedia — Tibialis anterior muscle
